CARDS. There are 24 cards in 4 suits: Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Bells. Each suit has Ace (11 card points), Ten (10), King (4), Ober (3), Unter (2) and Nine (0). The deck holds 120 card points.

MATCH. The match is 4 hands of 8 tricks each, one trick per round: 32 rounds. Both players start with 0 match points. Seat 1 has priority in hands 1 and 3. Seat 2 has priority in hands 2 and 4.

They are never seen by anyone, never played and never scored. 2) Sealed bid. Both players choose at the same moment exactly one of these 11 options: Pass; Wenz-Simple; Acorns-Simple; Leaves-Simple; Hearts-Simple; Bells-Simple; Wenz-Strong; Acorns-Strong; Leaves-Strong; Hearts-Strong; Bells-Strong. 3) Resolution. If both players pass, the hand is Ramsch and nobody is declarer. Otherwise Strong beats Simple, and any bid beats Pass. If both players bid at the same level (both Simple or both Strong), the priority player's bid wins whatever the contracts. The winning bidder is the declarer and the other player is the defender. The contract and level are those of the winning bid. 4) Both bids and the resulting contract (or Ramsch) are announced to both players. 5) Double. If the hand is not Ramsch, the defender chooses Double or No double. The choice is announced. Double doubles the stake; No double leaves it as it is. In Ramsch nobody is asked.

CONTRACTS. Wenz: the trumps are the 4 Unters only, ranked Acorns Unter > Leaves Unter > Hearts Unter > Bells Unter. In every suit the non-trump cards rank Ace > Ten > King > Ober > Nine. Unters belong to no plain suit. Suit Solo (Acorns, Leaves, Hearts or Bells, as named): there are 12 trumps, ranked from high to low: the four Obers (Acorns > Leaves > Hearts > Bells); then the four Unters (Acorns > Leaves > Hearts > Bells); then the Ace, Ten, King and Nine of the named suit. Obers and Unters belong to no plain suit. In the other three suits the non-trump cards rank Ace > Ten > King > Nine. Ramsch: trumps and ranks exactly as in Wenz.

TRICKS. 1) The leader plays any card from their hand. In the first trick of a hand the leader is the declarer, or the priority player in Ramsch. Afterwards the leader is the winner of the previous trick. 2) The other player then plays a card. If a trump was led, they must play a trump if they have one. If a plain suit was led, they must play a non-trump card of that suit if they have one. Otherwise they may play any card. You are offered only the cards you may legally play. 3) The trick is won by the highest trump in it. The stake is multiplied by 2 if the defender chose Double (Simple 4, Strong 8), and unchanged if not. If the contract is made, the declarer gains the stake. Otherwise the defender gains the stake. Ramsch: the player with fewer card points gains 1 match point. If the card points are equal, nobody scores. Card-point totals reset to 0 and the next hand begins.

END. After the fourth hand the match ends. The player with more match points wins. Equal match points is a draw (the win is shared).

[user]
=== Blind Officers' Schafkopf ===

CARDS. There are 24 cards in 4 suits: Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Bells. Each suit has Ace (11 card points), Ten (10), King (4), Ober (3), Unter (2) and Nine (0). The deck holds 120 card points.

MATCH. The match is 4 hands of 8 tricks each, one trick per round: 32 rounds. Both players start with 0 match points. Seat 1 has priority in hands 1 and 3. Seat 2 has priority in hands 2 and 4.

START OF EACH HAND. 1) Shuffle and deal 8 cards face down to each player. Each player sees only their own cards. The remaining 8 cards form the Blind. They are never seen by anyone, never played and never scored. 2) Sealed bid. Both players choose at the same moment exactly one of these 11 options: Pass; Wenz-Simple; Acorns-Simple; Leaves-Simple; Hearts-Simple; Bells-Simple; Wenz-Strong; Acorns-Strong; Leaves-Strong; Hearts-Strong; Bells-Strong. 3) Resolution. If both players pass, the hand is Ramsch and nobody is declarer. Otherwise Strong beats Simple, and any bid beats Pass. If both players bid at the same level (both Simple or both Strong), the priority player's bid wins whatever the contracts. The winning bidder is the declarer and the other player is the defender. The contract and level are those of the winning bid. 4) Both bids and the resulting contract (or Ramsch) are announced to both players. 5) Double. If the hand is not Ramsch, the defender chooses Double or No double. The choice is announced. Double doubles the stake; No double leaves it as it is. In Ramsch nobody is asked.

CONTRACTS. Wenz: the trumps are the 4 Unters only, ranked Acorns Unter > Leaves Unter > Hearts Unter > Bells Unter. In every suit the non-trump cards rank Ace > Ten > King > Ober > Nine. Unters belong to no plain suit. Suit Solo (Acorns, Leaves, Hearts or Bells, as named): there are 12 trumps, ranked from high to low: the four Obers (Acorns > Leaves > Hearts > Bells); then the four Unters (Acorns > Leaves > Hearts > Bells); then the Ace, Ten, King and Nine of the named suit. Obers and Unters belong to no plain suit. In the other three suits the non-trump cards rank Ace > Ten > King > Nine. Ramsch: trumps and ranks exactly as in Wenz.

TRICKS. 1) The leader plays any card from their hand. In the first trick of a hand the leader is the declarer, or the priority player in Ramsch. Afterwards the leader is the winner of the previous trick. 2) The other player then plays a card. If a trump was led, they must play a trump if they have one. If a plain suit was led, they must play a non-trump card of that suit if they have one. Otherwise they may play any card. You are offered only the cards you may legally play. 3) The trick is won by the highest trump in it. If it has no trump, it is won by the higher card of the led suit (a card of another suit never wins). 4) The trick winner adds the card points of both cards to their card-point total for the hand, and leads next. 5) The two cards, the trick winner and both players' card-point totals for the hand are announced.

END OF EACH HAND (after the 8th trick). Let D be the declarer's card points and F the defender's card points. A Simple contract is made if D >= F + 10; otherwise it fails. A Strong contract is made if D >= 2 x F and D >= 30; otherwise it fails. Stake: Simple is 2 match points and Strong is 4 match points. The stake is multiplied by 2 if the defender chose Double (Simple 4, Strong 8), and unchanged if not. If the contract is made, the declarer gains the stake. Otherwise the defender gains the stake. Ramsch: the player with fewer card points gains 1 match point. If the card points are equal, nobody scores. Card-point totals reset to 0 and the next hand begins.

END. After the fourth hand the match ends. The player with more match points wins. Equal match points is a draw (the win is shared).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

Each round runs in this order: shuffle and deal → your cards → sealed bid → resolve the bids → the bids are revealed → double → the double is announced → lead a card → follow a card → the trick is decided → the trick is announced → score the hand → the hand result → after the fourth hand.

  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told

You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
CARDS. There are 24 cards in 4 suits: Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Bells. Each suit has Ace (11 card points), Ten (10), King (4), Ober (3), Unter (2) and Nine (0). The deck holds 120 card points.

MATCH. The match is 4 hands of 8 tricks each, one trick per round: 32 rounds. Both players start with 0 match points. Seat 1 has priority in hands 1 and 3. Seat 2 has priority in hands 2 and 4.

START OF EACH HAND. 1) Shuffle and deal 8 cards face down to each player. Each player sees only their own cards. The remaining 8 cards form the Blind. They are never seen by anyone, never played and never scored. 2) Sealed bid. Both players choose at the same moment exactly one of these 11 options: Pass; Wenz-Simple; Acorns-Simple; Leaves-Simple; Hearts-Simple; Bells-Simple; Wenz-Strong; Acorns-Strong; Leaves-Strong; Hearts-Strong; Bells-Strong. 3) Resolution. If both players pass, the hand is Ramsch and nobody is declarer. Otherwise Strong beats Simple, and any bid beats Pass. If both players bid at the same level (both Simple or both Strong), the priority player's bid wins whatever the contracts. The winning bidder is the declarer and the other player is the defender. The contract and level are those of the winning bid. 4) Both bids and the resulting contract (or Ramsch) are announced to both players. 5) Double. If the hand is not Ramsch, the defender chooses Double or No double. The choice is announced. Double doubles the stake; No double leaves it as it is. In Ramsch nobody is asked.

CONTRACTS. Wenz: the trumps are the 4 Unters only, ranked Acorns Unter > Leaves Unter > Hearts Unter > Bells Unter. In every suit the non-trump cards rank Ace > Ten > King > Ober > Nine. Unters belong to no plain suit. Suit Solo (Acorns, Leaves, Hearts or Bells, as named): there are 12 trumps, ranked from high to low: the four Obers (Acorns > Leaves > Hearts > Bells); then the four Unters (Acorns > Leaves > Hearts > Bells); then the Ace, Ten, King and Nine of the named suit. Obers and Unters belong to no plain suit. In the other three suits the non-trump cards rank Ace > Ten > King > Nine. Ramsch: trumps and ranks exactly as in Wenz.

TRICKS. 1) The leader plays any card from their hand. In the first trick of a hand the leader is the declarer, or the priority player in Ramsch. Afterwards the leader is the winner of the previous trick. 2) The other player then plays a card. If a trump was led, they must play a trump if they have one. If a plain suit was led, they must play a non-trump card of that suit if they have one. Otherwise they may play any card. You are offered only the cards you may legally play. 3) The trick is won by the highest trump in it. If it has no trump, it is won by the higher card of the led suit (a card of another suit never wins). 4) The trick winner adds the card points of both cards to their card-point total for the hand, and leads next. 5) The two cards, the trick winner and both players' card-point totals for the hand are announced.

END OF EACH HAND (after the 8th trick). Let D be the declarer's card points and F the defender's card points. A Simple contract is made if D >= F + 10; otherwise it fails. A Strong contract is made if D >= 2 x F and D >= 30; otherwise it fails. Stake: Simple is 2 match points and Strong is 4 match points. The stake is multiplied by 2 if the defender chose Double (Simple 4, Strong 8), and unchanged if not. If the contract is made, the declarer gains the stake. Otherwise the defender gains the stake. Ramsch: the player with fewer card points gains 1 match point. If the card points are equal, nobody scores. Card-point totals reset to 0 and the next hand begins.

END. After the fourth hand the match ends. The player with more match points wins. Equal match points is a draw (the win is shared).
